editorial.headline: Repairing the Home, Meeting Bali’s PMA Block
editorial.standfirst: This repair and maintenance activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but Bali’s permanent low- and medium-low-risk moratorium blocks PMA registration today.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this activity in Bali today. Nationally, it is classified as open to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. Bali reaches a different result: the record marks the activity as blocked for PMA registration under the province’s island-wide, permanent moratorium for low- and medium-low-risk activities. The applicable Bali moratorium is dated May 13, 2026.

The work itself is practical, familiar and broad within the household setting. It covers repair and maintenance services for domestic equipment including refrigerators, stoves, washing machines, clothes dryers, air conditioners, electric irons, vacuum cleaners and other electrical household goods and furnishings. It also reaches home and garden equipment: lawn mowers, edgers, snow and leaf sweepers, trimmers and similar items. The boundaries are equally clear. Powered hand tools and centralised air-conditioning systems sit outside this activity’s stated scope.

The activity is open across every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That makes it a defined service category rather than one reserved for a particular size of operator. Its national foreign-investment position is equally direct: TERBUKA, with the full 100% ceiling recorded under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a founder considering the activity at national level, those are the terms stated in the record.

Bali requires a separate reading, not a softer interpretation of the national position. The record identifies the OSS risk at the Besar scale, across every scope, as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah. Bali’s rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk activities from PMA registration, island-wide and permanently. The result is therefore unambiguous for a foreign-owned setup in Bali: although the national ceiling is 100%, this activity is blocked from PMA registration there today. National openness does not turn a Bali PMA block into permission.
